claim_tested: Members of the ABHD14 family are catalytically active serine hydrolases
key_finding: Soluble N-terminally truncated human ABHD14A turns over short-chain esters in gel-based ABPP and p-nitrophenyl-ester assays, with CoA-dependent enhancement of pNP-acetate hydrolysis indicating ping-pong acetyl transfer; ABHD14A-GFP localises to the Golgi
context: human ABHD14A, recombinant protein and HEK293T cells
confidence_limits: high for human ABHD14A; engineered truncation, in vitro surrogate substrate, no nematode protein tested

claim_tested: Human ABHD14B has catalytic activity through its Ser-Asp-His triad
key_finding: ABHD14B acts as a lysine deacetylase transferring acetyl to coenzyme A
confidence_limits: high for human ABHD14B; vertebrate paralog-specific, arose after the duplication that excludes nematodes

claim_tested: ABHD14B/CIB has hydrolase activity and modulates transcription
key_finding: Source of GO:0016787 IDA, GO:0005515 IPI and GO:0045944 IDA on Q96IU4
confidence_limits: the transcription readout is downstream and paralog-specific; not transferable to worm

claim_tested: Reference geometry of an assembled ABHD14 catalytic triad
key_finding: Ser111-Asp162-His188 at 2.84 and 2.73 A, elbow phi/psi +40.4/-118.2, oxyanion donors Leu112 N 2.79 A and Ile41 N 4.97 A, cavity 246 A^3
confidence_limits: experimental reference; apo form, no bound substrate

citation: This analysis, AlphaFold DB v6 model of Q9N366
claim_tested: C. elegans ABHD-14 retains an assembled, solvent-accessible catalytic triad
key_finding: Ser145-Asp193-His220, Ser OG to His NE2 3.04 A, His ND1 to Asp OD 2.88 A, Ser CA to His CA 8.40 A, elbow phi/psi +52.4/-116.5, oxyanion donors Met146 N 2.99 A and Gln79 N 5.27 A, cavity 291 A^3, 10-atom anchor superposition onto 1IMJ 0.37 A RMSD, local pLDDT 96.7-97.9
context: AlphaFold prediction, no experimental worm structure
confidence_limits: a model; high pLDDT and crystal-matching geometry, but geometry alone does not prove turnover

citation: This analysis, 65 nematode orthologs from UniProt
claim_tested: The triad is maintained by selection across Nematoda
key_finding: Ser145 96.9%, His220 95.4%, Asp193 93.8% identical; HG motif His77 92.3% and Gly78 87.7%; oxyanion Met146 78.5% and Gln79 83.1%
confidence_limits: sequence conservation implies maintained function, not which substrate

citation: This analysis, 2347 UniProt entries with PANTHER PTHR46197
claim_tested: C. elegans ABHD-14 is specifically the ortholog of human ABHD14B
key_finding: SF1 (853) and SF2 (901) are 1754/1754 vertebrate with zero non-vertebrate members; SF3 is 592 non-vertebrate plus 1 vertebrate outlier; tunicates, amphioxus, echinoderms and hemichordates are all SF3; Fisher exact odds inf, p < 1e-300. Q9N366 is SF3
confidence_limits: depends on PANTHER subfamily assignment quality; the clade signal is absolute, so misassignment of a few entries would not change it

citation: This analysis, neighbour-joining tree of 16 representatives
claim_tested: C. elegans ABHD-14 groups with either vertebrate paralog
key_finding: Vertebrate ABHD14A+ABHD14B monophyletic at 54.5% bootstrap (ABHD14A 97.0%, ABHD14B 100.0%); Ce_ABHD-14 sits outside it in a 100%-supported nematode clade; nearest non-nematode neighbours are cnidarian (1.241) and mollusc (1.332), closer than any vertebrate paralog (1.319-1.417)
context: centre-star alignment, 210 columns, Kimura-corrected p-distance, 200 bootstraps
confidence_limits: distance method on 210 columns; deep internodes have 2.5-5.0% support, so invertebrate branching order is unresolved

citation: This analysis, global Needleman-Wunsch with BLOSUM62
claim_tested: ABHD-14 is closer to one human paralog than the other
key_finding: 34.9% identity to ABHD14A and 35.0% to ABHD14B (A vs B 45.9%); at the 112 columns where A and B differ, the worm matches A at 18 and B at 19, binomial p = 1.00
confidence_limits: single alignment method; the tie is wide, not marginal

claim_tested: ABHD-14 shares ABHD14A's membrane anchor and Golgi targeting
key_finding: Max KD-19 for Q9N366 is 1.56 with 0 windows above 1.6, matching ABHD14B (1.53) and unlike ABHD14A (2.40 at residue 44, 8 windows)
confidence_limits: hydropathy heuristic, not a TM predictor consensus or an experiment

citation: ESTHER database, gene_locus caeel-Y55F3AM.10 and human-ABHD14A
claim_tested: Independent alpha/beta-hydrolase classification of the worm protein
key_finding: Both assigned family CIB-CCG1-interacting-factor-B, a label carrying ABHD14B's alias; drome-CG2059 returns a different family, so the lookup discriminates. human-ABHD14B, mouse-Abhd14a and mouse-Abhd14b returned HTTP 500 and could not be read
confidence_limits: family-level only; the name invites ABHD14B function carry-over that the phylogeny does not support

claim_tested: Current annotation state of C. elegans abhd-14
key_finding: Only GO:0005737 cytoplasm, IBA GO_REF:0000033 and IEA GO_REF:0000044. No MF, no BP. UniProt entry is TrEMBL, annotation score 1.0, protein existence 3
confidence_limits: confirms the gene is uncharacterised; no evidence is being overwritten

claim_tested: Experimental characterisation of C. elegans abhd-14 exists
key_finding: 10 hits returned, none about this gene. No assay, mutant, RNAi or localisation study found
confidence_limits: absence of evidence in PubMed; WormBase REST and the Alliance search API were not reachable from this environment, so phenotype databases were not checked

citation: This analysis, nucleophile elbow sequence read from four structures
claim_tested: The seed hypothesis premise that a GxSxG motif marks the elbow
key_finding: No ABHD14 protein has GxSxG. Human ABHD14A and ABHD14B both read S-P-S-L-S-G around the catalytic Ser; C. elegans reads C-A-S-M-A-A. All four adopt the strained epsilon elbow conformation anyway
confidence_limits: a GxSxG regex would misclassify all three proteins as non-catalytic
